options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --ontology ONTOLOGY
  --data DATA
  --import-dir IMPORT_DIR
                        searched recursively for local copies of imports
                        (default: the ontology file's own directory)
  --exclude-imports     evaluate the ontology file alone; owl:imports are
                        neither fetched nor merged
  --allow-network       fetch an unresolved owl:imports IRI over HTTP (off by
                        default)
  --shapes SHAPES
  --sparql SPARQL       a directory of .rq check queries, or @builtin for the
                        suite's own tree wherever this install put it.
                        Repeatable: pass it more than once to run a project's
                        own checks alongside the suite's, which is what you
                        almost always want. Given at all, it replaces the
                        built-in tree, so `--sparql mine` runs only yours --
                        the run warns when that happens. See
                        docs/EXTENDING.md.
  --registry REGISTRY
  --themes THEMES       a JSON or CSV map of check id to a question in your
                        own words, used to add a "by question" index to
                        findings.txt -- see docs/REPORTS.md
  --inference {none,rdfs}
                        materialise an RDFS closure before the checks run.
                        Applied once to the graph both formulations read, so
                        --engine sparql, shacl and both all see it and agree;
                        it used to be a parameter of the SHACL arm alone,
                        which left the two arms checking different graphs and
                        did nothing at all under --engine sparql. Expect
                        findings to move in both directions: entailed triples
                        reveal some and resolve others. 'owlrl'/'both' are
                        gone -- the SHACL engine has no OWL2-RL reasoner, and
                        the OWL2-RL closure is its own stage
                        (reasoning/backends/owlrl_backend.py).
  --engine {both,sparql,shacl,native,native+sparql}
                        which formulation of the registry-driven suite to run.
                        'both' runs the SHACL shapes and the portable SPARQL
                        layer and cross-checks them for drift; 'sparql' runs
                        the portable layer alone -- every check has a SPARQL
                        form, so it finds the same real findings without the
                        drift signal; 'shacl' runs the shapes alone. 'native'
                        and 'native+sparql' are older spellings of 'shacl' and
                        'both', kept because scripts pass them. Every SHACL
                        spelling runs the `shacl` engine, which is a runtime
                        dependency: pyshacl is now a test-only second opinion
                        (tests/test_engine_parity_stress.py) and no engine
                        choice selects it.
  --out-dir OUT_DIR
  --reports {all,minimal}
                        which report files to write under --out-dir: 'all'
                        (default) writes findings.txt, full_results.csv,
                        report.html, cucumber.json, features/ and plots/;
                        'minimal' writes findings.txt and full_results.csv
                        only -- the one for a person and the one for a script
                        -- and skips the plotting, which is most of the time a
                        small run spends
  --fail-on {Violation,Warning,Info,never}
  --own-namespace OWN_NAMESPACE
                        only show findings whose focus node starts with this
                        IRI prefix (repeatable-free; a single prefix, e.g.
                        'https://example.org/acme/'). Filters the report, it
                        does not change what's checked -- imports are still
                        resolved and reasoned over normally, so a finding in
                        your own terms that depends on an imported
                        vocabulary's declarations is still caught. Unlike
                        --exclude-imports, this does not introduce undeclared-
                        term noise; it just hides pre-existing findings that
                        belong to an imported vocabulary rather than your own.
  -v, --verbose         print what each input option actually resolved to
                        before running: which query/data files --query-
                        pattern/--data-pattern matched, which owl:imports
                        resolved (and from where) or failed to, and which
                        check engine ran
